title: Small acts
hook: love is mostly in small things

segments.voice: Yesterday, loving yourself rightly, and Queen Mallika's honest answer. Your line was me too. What kind thing did you do for yourself? Today, love shrinks down to fit in a cup. Day eight hundred seventy-one.

Drip. Drip. A leaky faucet over a bucket, or rain off the edge of a roof into a clay pot. Each drop is almost nothing. Nobody would bother to measure one. Leave the pot there overnight, though, and in the morning it's full to the brim. A verse in the Dhammapada, an old collection of the Buddha's sayings, uses exactly that picture, and not for water. For goodness. Three traditions speak to how small love can be and still count. Today: small acts.
screen: `DRIP. DRIP.` → `EACH DROP IS ALMOST NOTHING.` → `IN THE MORNING, A FULL POT.`

segments.voice: First, the water-pot. In Max Müller's translation of the Dhammapada, the verse warns against thinking lightly of good, as if it could never add up to much. Then comes the picture: "Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled." The wise, it says, become full of good the same way, gathering it little by little. No single drop fills the pot. Every drop is part of the filling. Second, a cup of water. In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus says that whoever gives "a cup of cold water only" to one of his little ones, in the name of a disciple, "shall in no wise lose his reward." Notice the word only. Not a banquet. Not a fortune. Just water, and cold, which in a hot land is its own kindness. The smallest gift on the table, and Jesus says it isn't lost. Third, a face. A saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, recorded in the collection of al-Tirmidhi, says in plain words that your smile in the face of your brother is charity. Charity, here, isn't only money. A smile counts. So does, in the same saying, guiding someone who is lost, or moving a stone out of the road. Fourth, what the three share, each in its own words. None of them says big acts don't matter. They say small ones aren't nothing. A text back. A door held. The dishes done without being asked. On an ordinary day, love often looks like that, and these teachers say it adds up.
screen: `A WATER-POT, DROP BY DROP.` · `A CUP OF COLD WATER ONLY.` · `A SMILE IS CHARITY.` · `SMALL ISN'T NOTHING.` · then, large: `SMALL ACTS.`

segments.voice: Breathe in, and breathe out slowly. As you breathe, let the day ahead come to mind, the places you'll be and the people you'll see. Now choose three small kindnesses that fit inside it. Not plans that need a calendar, just drops. A glass of water poured for someone. A real smile at the person at the counter. A message that says thinking of you. See each one clearly, one at a time, the way a drop falls. If you pray, you can offer the day in your own tradition's words. The bell holds the time.
Small acts. Kindnesses too small to measure one by one, the drop, the cup of water, the smile, that fill the pot over time. Today's word.
Your line: small things. Do three small kindnesses today, and don't wait for any of them to feel important. Count them if you like, drop by drop. Day eight hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Buddhists speak of gathering merit little by little through everyday good deeds, Christians read the cup of cold water as a picture of small service, and the hadith in al-Tirmidhi counts a smile or removing harm from a path among acts of charity.

fork.setup: a stranger looks lost in the street, and you have nothing to give but a few seconds. in the saying recorded by al-Tirmidhi, what counts as charity here?
options: nothing, without money it doesn't count.
a smile and showing them the way.
only a prayer for them later.
fork.reveal: the saying counts a smile as charity, and guiding someone who is lost too. the smallest gifts are on the list.

trapdoor: what you thought: love means big gestures.
what it means: love is mostly carried in small acts, and small acts add up.
what a scholar hears: Dhammapada 122's water-pot, Matthew 10:42's cup of cold water, and Tirmidhi's smile as charity, three texts making the same small point in their own words.
